2. Counter affidavit filed by learned counsel for the informant is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Upendra Upadhyay, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Dinesh Prasad Rajbhar, learned counsel for the informant, Sri R.P. Patel, learned State Law Officer for the State and perused the material placed on record.
4.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.141 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Nonhara, District-Ghazipur with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
5. As per prosecution story, the marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased person as per Hindu Rites on 10.05.2023.

The applicant and other family members are stated to have subjected the deceased to cruelty for demand of motorcycle, cash and golden ornaments as dowry,
thereby leading her to death on 25.08.2023 at about 10 AM.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the FIR is delayed and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
Cause of death could not be ascertained, as such, Viscera was preserved and chemical analysis of Viscera indicates the presence of Aluminum Phosphide in it.
It is further argued that it was a love marriage between the parties, as such, there is no question of demand of dowry.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is in jail since 28.08.2023 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant and learned State Law Officer have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the FIR is prompt applicant is the husband and the deceased expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant as such, he is not entitled for bail.
8. This Court had called for status of trial from the trial court concerned.
As per the status report dated 14.08.2025 received from the trial court concerned, two witnesses have been examined.

9. The Supreme Court in case of X vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr., 2024 INSC 909, has held that once the trial has commenced, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion, which may either result in conviction or acquittal of the accused.

sentences.text: The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.

It should also not be granted by looking into the Vipin Bind vs State Of U.P. on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111171687/
2 discrepancies here or there in the deposition.

sentences.text: 10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the promptness of FIR which was instituted within four hours of the incident and the deceased expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
11. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

12. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgments of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
